reasoning: Both attempts implement the rules and the timing correctly. A passes every check, uses the closed BlockType type for parameters and an optional per-player map, and names its yielding loader with Async. B has a load retry and runtime validation, but it has luau-lsp errors in its own code, takes blockType as unknown so misspellings aren't caught by the checker, doesn't mark the per-player map as optional, and breaks the project conventions. A is the one a developer could merge as-is.

criteria.note: loadCountsAsync uses DATA_STORE_NAME "BlockInventory" and `player_{UserId}`, createStartingCounts gives 20 each, TakeBlock stops at 0, ReturnBlock stops at MAX_HELD_COUNT 99, GrantBlocks has no cap, GetCount reads a count, and onPlayerRemoving clears the player.

The activePlayers flag is checked after loadCountsAsync so counts aren't stored for a player who left, existing players are loaded through task.spawn, and every function returns NotLoaded or nil for a missing player.
It returns (false, "NotLoaded"/"OutOfBlocks"/"AtLimit"), asserts only on caller mistakes (bad amount or unknown type), and wraps the DataStore load in pcall with a fallback to the starting counts.
Parameters are typed blockType: BlockType, returns are typed with per-function failure unions, and countsByPlayer is typed { [Player]: Counts? }.
Going past the cap uses the separate GrantBlocks function, and the yielding loader is named loadCountsAsync.
It is a single module with no remotes or saving, reuses BlockTypes, and passes luau-lsp, selene, and StyLua; the DataStore check failure is a false negative because the name is in a constant.

It uses DATASTORE_NAME "BlockInventory" and getKey `player_{UserId}`, gives StartingCount 20, take stops at 0, giveBack stops at MaxCount 99, grant is uncapped, getCount reads a count, and onPlayerRemoving clears the player.
It checks player.Parent ~= Players after the load to skip players who left, uses a loading set to avoid loading twice, loads existing players through task.spawn, and resolve() returns NotLoaded.
The FailReason union covers NotLoaded, OutOfBlocks, and AtLimit, and loadSaved uses pcall with retries and falls back to the starting counts.
Public functions take blockType: unknown, so a misspelled type isn't a type error, and states is typed { [Player]: PlayerState } without the optional marker.
The separate grant function handles going past the cap, but the yielding loader loadSaved has no Async suffix.
luau-lsp reports type errors in its own code at lines 62 and 83, and it breaks the project conventions (local instead of const, an instance-path require, a returned table not named Module).

strengths: Clean strict typing using the closed BlockType set and an optional per-player map
Correctly guards against storing counts for a player who left mid-load
Separate GrantBlocks function for gives that go past the cap, and specific failure-reason types per function
All checks pass and it follows the project conventions
weaknesses: Method-call syntax (Module:) is unnecessary for a stateless module
No load retry and no record of a failed load to protect later saving

strengths: Load retry, and a loadFailed flag that will protect saving later
Runtime validation of block type and amount comes back as return values
Thorough handling of leave-during-load and double loading
weaknesses: Fails luau-lsp type analysis in its own code
unknown blockType parameters lose the type safety of the closed BlockType set
The per-player map isn't typed as optional
